rapit: rapiō, -ere, rapuī, raptum — to seize, snatch, hurry along (3rd sg. pres.)
raptum: rapiō, -ere, rapuī, raptum — to seize, snatch, carry off (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg.)
rebusque: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, affair, matter; pl. circumstances (dat./abl. pl.) + -que, and
reducta: redūcō, -ere, -dūxī, -ductum — to draw back, pull back (perf. part., f. abl. sg.; also f. nom. sg., n. nom./acc. pl.)
referens: referō, referre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back, tell again (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
rerum: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (gen. pl.)
rigat: rigō, -āre — to water, irrigate (3rd sg. pres.)
rubra: ruber, -bra, -brum — red, ruddy (f. abl. sg.; also f. nom. sg., n. nom./acc. pl.)
ruentem: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, fall headlong, collapse (pres. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
ruit: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.)
rutuli: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Rutulians, people of Turnus in Latium (nom. pl.); Rutulus, -ī, a Rutulian (gen. sg.) · also m. voc. pl. (O Rutuli)
rutulis: Rutulī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Rutulians, people of Latium under Turnus (dat./abl. pl.)
ruunt: ruō, ruere, ruī — to rush, tumble; trans. to churn up, upheave (3rd pl. pres.)
salutant: salūtō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to greet, hail (3rd pl. pres.)
salutem: salūs, salūtis (f.) — safety, welfare, deliverance (acc. sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
secat: secō, -āre, secuī, sectum — to cut, cut off, sever (3rd sg. pres.)
securi: secūris, -is (f.) — axe (abl. sg., -ī form) · also sēcūrus, -a, -um — free from care, untroubled (m. nom. pl., + gen.: sēcūrī pelagī)
secutus: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue (perf. part., m. nom. sg., deponent)
sequens: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue; to seek (pres. part., m./f. nom. sg.)
sermonem: sermō, -ōnis (m.) — talk, speech, conversation, discourse (acc. sg.)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
sibi: suī (reflexive pron.) — to/for himself, herself, themselves (dat.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
signum: signum, -ī (n.) — sign, token, standard (acc. sg.) · also nom. sg. (tessera signum, the watchword)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sonantem: sonō, -āre, -uī, -itum — to sound, ring, resound (pres. part., m. acc. sg.) · also f. acc. sg. (turbam sonantem)
soror: soror, sorōris (f.) — sister (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg. (Anna soror)
sortem: sors, sortis (f.) — lot, chance; fate (acc. sg.)
strictis: stringō, -ere, strīnxī, strictum — to draw, strip off; strictus, drawn (perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl.)
subiciunt: subiciō, subicere, subiēcī, subiectum — to put under, set beneath (3rd pl. pres.)
subito: subitō (adv.) — suddenly; also subitus, -a, -um, sudden (abl./dat. sg.)
sumus: sum, esse, fuī — to be (1st pl. pres.)
sunt: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there are; sunt mihi, I have (3rd pl. pres.)
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
superbis: superbus, -a, -um — proud, splendid, lordly (n. abl. pl.) · also f. abl. pl. (ratibus superbīs, 'proud ships'; m./f./n. dat./abl. pl.)
superos: superī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the gods above (acc. pl.)
suppliciter: suppliciter (adv.) — humbly, as suppliants, in supplication
sutilis: sūtilis, -e — sewn, stitched together (f. nom. sg.; cymba sūtilis, a skiff of hide)
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tela: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (acc./nom. pl.)
teloque: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear (abl. sg.) + -que, and
telorum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, weapon, spear, dart (gen. pl.)
telum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, spear, arrow, weapon (acc./nom. sg.)
tempestas: tempestās, tempestātis (f.) — storm, weather, season (nom. sg.)
teritur: terō, -ere, trīvī, trītum — to rub, wear away, spend (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
terrae: terra, -ae (f.) — earth, land, country (gen./dat. sg.; nom. pl.)
territat: territō, -āre — to frighten, terrify (3rd sg. pres.)
tolumnius: Tolumnius, -ī (m.) — Tolumnius, Rutulian augur and ally of Turnus (nom. sg.)
troes: Trōs, Trōis (m.) — a Trojan (nom. pl., Greek form Trōes)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbamque: turba, -ae (f.) — crowd, throng, multitude (acc. sg.) + -que, and
turbati: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to disturb, throw into confusion (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl., with animī)
turbavit: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to disturb, throw into disorder, scatter (3rd sg. perf.)
turbida: turbidus, -a, -um — stormy, turbulent, confused (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
turni: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli, Latinus's rival for Lavinia (gen. sg.)
turno: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutuli (dat. sg., Turnō, 'to Turnus'; also abl. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
tyrrhena: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Tyrrhenian, Etruscan (f. abl. sg.; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
tyrrhenum: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Tyrrhenian, Etruscan; the Tyrrhenian sea west of Italy (n./m. acc. sg.)
ullum: ullus, -a, -um — any (n. nom./acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.)
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
unam: ūnus, -a, -um — one, one alone, single (f. acc. sg.)
uncis: uncus, -a, -um — hooked, curved, crooked (m./f./n. abl. pl.)
unguibus: unguis, -is (m.) — nail, claw, talon (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
unum: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single, the same (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
unus: ūnus, -a, -um — one, alone, a single (m. nom. sg.)
urget: urgeō, -ēre, ursī — to press, push hard, urge on, bear down on (3rd sg. pres.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent) · also + subj., oh that (wish: ut … ludar)
varios: varius, -a, -um — various, diverse, changing (m. acc. pl.)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
vestra: vester, vestra, vestrum — your (pl.) (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vi: vīs (f.; acc. vim, abl. vī) — force, power, violence (abl. sg.)
victus: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, overcome (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
videri: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see; pass. to be seen, seem (pres. pass. inf.)
vidit: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. perf.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
virtutis: virtūs, -ūtis (f.) — manly excellence, valour, courage (gen. sg.)
visu: vīsus, -ūs (m.) — sight, seeing (abl. sg.; miserābile vīsū, pitiable to see)
vobis: tū, tuī — you; vōs, vōbīs, to/for you, by you (dat./abl. pl.)
volans: volō, -āre — to fly (pres. part., m. nom. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (columba volāns)
volgi: volgus (vulgus), -ī (n.) — the common people, crowd (gen. sg.)
volucres: volucris, -is (f.) — bird, winged creature (nom./acc. pl.) · also adj., winged, swift (f. acc. pl.: volucrēs aurās)
volunt: volō, velle, voluī — to wish, want, be willing (3rd pl. pres.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
